Neha — quick status: (short answers inline)

1) SSO: SAML 2.0 + SCIM multitenant IdP — Supported in Hosted API for single IdP today. SCIM user provisioning exists but multi-IdP per tenant is not first-class; we can do workarounds (routing + tenant mapping) for pilot within 2–3 weeks. Risk: edge-case role sync.

2) BYOK (AWS KMS / CloudHSM) private deployments — Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS for storage encryption. Full envelope-key rotation with per-tenant BYOK and HSM-backed signing will need a short roadmap item (~4–6 weeks) to validate HSM integration and key lifecycle APIs. Risk: audit of key access paths.

3) Audit logs: 7-year retention + immutable export — Our default retention is 1 year in hosted logs store; dedicated/private can export logs to customer S3. Immutable, tamper-evident storage (WORM) is not implemented; we can deliver export + lifecycle hooks in ~3 weeks for pilot but immutable retention will need a compliance add-on & platform changes (~8–12 weeks).

4) Granular admin audit access / delegation — Basic RBAC exists, but audit-specific delegated roles are not granular enough. We can add delegated read-only audit roles in ~2 weeks for pilot.

Summary (short): SSO multi-IdP and BYOK full HSM support and immutable WORM retention are the main gaps. Proposed pilot scope: temporary exception for immutable retention (customer-hosted S3 with object lock) + workaround for multi-IdP.

-Dev

Subject: RE: Requirements: SSO + BYOK + audit retention for pilot

Thanks — adding security perspective and compliance constraints.

- BYOK/KMS: For private deployments we can support customer-managed keys for disk and DB encryption today, but not all crypto operations (signing/token encryption) are offloaded to customer HSMs. If Acme insists on HSM for signing, we'll need an exception workflow and an architectural review. That adds time.

- Audit logs: 7-year retention is OK if logs are exported to the customer's S3 with object-lock (WORM) and we provide a signed export manifest monthly. The requirement we need validated: do regulators require us to operate the WORM storage or is customer-managed acceptable? If customer-managed is acceptable, we can deliver a pilot solution fast (3 weeks).

- SSO/SCIM: Confirm that Acme's IdP supports SCIM push and has stable identifiers for mapping. Also want to confirm whether SCIM will be used for provision-only or provisioning + deprovisioning.

Operational ask: if we provide a short-term exception (customer-managed WORM + attestations), we need a documented runbook and legal signoff. I can draft the runbook once we confirm acceptance.

-Hannah

Priya / Acme team — thanks for the checklist and patience while we coordinated internally. Short summary and proposed path forward: 

1) SSO / SCIM multi-IdP: Workaround available for pilot (routing + SCIM provisioning). ETA: 2–3 weeks for configuration + testing.

2) BYOK / KMS: Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS for storage; HSM-backed signing is roadmap-only. Proposal: pilot uses customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest; full HSM signing targeted in 4–6 weeks with a signed milestone in the Statement of Work.

3) Audit logs (7-year retention + immutable): Short-term solution: export audit logs to Acme S3 with Object Lock enabled; Redwood provides a monthly signed manifest and retention policy documentation. ETA: 3 weeks. Long-term: platform-level WORM and immutable audit store (8–12 weeks).

4) Granular admin audit access: Add delegated read-only audit roles for the pilot. ETA: ~2 weeks.

Commercial: Marissa will circulate pilot terms (exception + acceptance criteria) and include milestone/date commitments. Legal/procurement target: Mar 10 for signed terms to match Acme timeline.
